Schnittstelle Fun<X,Y>

Typparameter:
X - the input type
Y - the output type
Alle Superschnittstellen:
Applicable<X,Y>, Deferrable<X,Y>, Function<X,Y>
Alle bekannten Unterschnittstellen:
MemoisingFun<X,Y>, Operator<A>, Provider<A>, Receiver<A>
Funktionsschnittstelle:
Dies ist eine funktionale Schnittstelle, die somit als Zuweisungsziel für einen Lambdaausdruck oder eine Methodenreferenz verwendet werden kann.
@FunctionalInterface public interface Fun<X,Y> extends Function<X,Y>, Applicable<X,Y>

A functional interface that extends Function with stronger contracts and convenient combinators such as composition, memoization, and null-safety wrappers.

Compared to the JDK's Function, this interface adopts a stricter non-null contract: unless explicitly stated otherwise, inputs must not be null and results must not be null. Helper methods like fun(Function) and nullSafe() make these guarantees explicit.

Side effects: Functions created or used via Fun are not required to be pure or referentially transparent. They may have side effects and may produce different results over time. If you need memoization with stable semantics, use MemoisingFun only with pure functions.

Seit:
1.0.0

  • Methodendetails

    • fun

      static <X,Y> Fun<X,Y> fun(@NonNull Function<X,Y> function)

      Creates a new Fun from the given Function, enforcing non-null input and output.

      Contract: function must not be null; applying the returned Fun will throw a NullPointerException if the input is null or if the wrapped function returns null.

      Typparameter:
      X - the input type
      Y - the output type
      Parameter:
      function - the function to wrap; must not be null
      Gibt zurück:
      a Fun that enforces the non-null contract
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • apply

      @Pure @NonNull Y apply(@NonNull X x)

      Applies this function to the provided input.

      Contract: x must not be null; the result must not be null. Implementations can rely on wrappers like fun(Function) or nullSafe() to enforce this at runtime.

      Angegeben von:
      apply in Schnittstelle Applicable<X,Y>
      Angegeben von:
      apply in Schnittstelle Function<X,Y>
      Parameter:
      x - the input; must not be null
      Gibt zurück:
      the result; never null
      Löst aus:
      NullPointerException - if x is null or the implementation returns null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • compose

      default <W> @NonNull Fun<W,Y> compose(@NonNull Fun<? super W, ? extends X> first)

      Returns a function representing the composition this ∘ first. The resulting function first applies first, then applies this.

      Contract: first must not be null; both first and this must not return null.

      Typparameter:
      W - the input type of first
      Parameter:
      first - the function to apply before this one; must not be null
      Gibt zurück:
      the composed function
      Löst aus:
      NullPointerException - if first is null or any intermediate result is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • andThen

      default <Z> @NonNull Fun<X,Z> andThen(@NonNull Fun<? super Y, ? extends Z> next)

      Returns a function representing the composition next ∘ this. The resulting function first applies this, then applies next.

      Contract: next must not be null; both this and next must not return null.

      Typparameter:
      Z - the output type of the resulting function
      Parameter:
      next - the function to apply after this one; must not be null
      Gibt zurück:
      the composed function
      Löst aus:
      NullPointerException - if next is null or any intermediate result is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • memoise

      default MemoisingFun<X,Y> memoise()

      Returns a memoized view of this function that caches results by input.

      Contract:

      • The returned function must never return null.
      • Cache semantics assume referential transparency for equal inputs. Using this on non‑pure/side‑effecting functions can yield surprising results and is not recommended.
      Gibt zurück:
      a memoizing wrapper of this function
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • nullSafe

      default Fun<X,Y> nullSafe()

      Returns a null-checking wrapper around this function that rejects null inputs and results with NullPointerException.

      Gibt zurück:
      a null-safe wrapper of this function
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • identity

      static <X> Fun<X,X> identity()

      Returns a strict identity function, rejecting null inputs.

      This is stricter than Function.identity() which allows null. Here, a NullPointerException is thrown if the input is null.

      Typparameter:
      X - the input/output type
      Gibt zurück:
      an identity function for type X
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • async

      default @NonNull Fun<Supplier<X>, CompletableFuture<Y>> async()

      Returns a function that applies this function asynchronously to a value supplied lazily.

      Execution context: The returned function automatically selects an appropriate ForkJoinPool for execution when applied. If the calling thread is a ForkJoinWorkerThread, the computation is submitted to that thread's associated pool. Otherwise, execution is delegated to ForkJoinPool.commonPool().

      Gibt zurück:
      a function that accepts a Supplier and returns a CompletableFuture
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • async

      default @NonNull Fun<Supplier<X>, CompletableFuture<Y>> async(@NonNull ExecutorService executor)

      Returns a function that applies this function asynchronously using the provided ExecutorService.

      This overload provides explicit control over the execution context.

      Parameter:
      executor - the executor to use; must not be null
      Gibt zurück:
      a function that accepts a Supplier and returns a CompletableFuture
      Löst aus:
      NullPointerException - if executor is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • deferredAsync

      default @NonNull Fun<Supplier<X>, Provider<CompletableFuture<Y>>> deferredAsync()

      Returns a function that prepares a deferred asynchronous computation.

      The returned function takes a value supplier and returns a Provider (a supplier of futures). Invoking the provider submits the task for execution.

      Execution context: Uses the same automatic pool selection logic as async().

      Gibt zurück:
      a function yielding a Provider for the deferred computation
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • deferredAsync

      default Fun<Supplier<X>, Provider<CompletableFuture<Y>>> deferredAsync(@NonNull ExecutorService executor)

      Returns a function that prepares a deferred asynchronous computation using the provided ExecutorService.

      The returned function takes a value supplier and returns a Provider. Invoking the provider submits the task to the specified executor.

      Parameter:
      executor - the executor to use; must not be null
      Gibt zurück:
      a function yielding a Provider for the deferred computation
      Löst aus:
